title: Atlas Studio
description: Design systems and digital experiences for ambitious small teams.

sections.title: Frontend structure that stays elegant as the site grows.
sections.copy: Atlas Studio helps small teams ship editorial marketing sites with stronger hierarchy, cleaner systems, and fewer redesign spirals. The output is static, fast, and easy to extend.

panel.title: Codette patterns are built to stay reusable.
items: Plain HTML and CSS with tiny JS only when needed

sections.title: A slow-growing collection of layouts with clear input contracts.
sections.copy: The point is not to stockpile components. The point is to keep a short list of sections that solve real brochure-site problems well.

items.title: Hero Systems
items.copy: Headline-led intros with supporting proof, action clusters, and optional side panels.

items.title: Editorial Grids
items.copy: Feature groupings, asymmetric content blocks, and rhythm that survives real content.

items.title: Conversion Bands
items.copy: Clear CTA sections that feel deliberate instead of bolted onto the page.

sections.title: Structured preview rows for articles, notes, or featured writing.
sections.copy: This pattern comes from the content-led rhythm in Amplified Expansion Coaching and can also support an editorial magazine front page.

items.title: Design systems feel smaller when the section grammar is stable.
items.copy: A preview row works well when a site needs to surface current writing without collapsing into a generic blog card grid.

items.title: Editorial layouts need stronger rhythm than generic component stacks.
items.copy: Alternating emphasis, disciplined typography, and image-aware spacing matter more than sheer component count.

sections.title: Image-plus-copy split sections translate cleanly from both source sites.
sections.copy: One side carries the visual atmosphere, the other carries persuasion, proof, and the next action. That makes it useful for about blocks, event promos, or press features.
points: Supports plain content pages and marketing homepages.
Can reverse media placement without changing content structure.
Stays compatible with real images or placeholder media blocks.

sections.title: A Codette-native carousel for image-led editorial storytelling.
sections.copy: This replaces the old Bootstrap dependency with a smaller reusable pattern. It supports captions, controls, indicators, and optional autoplay.

slides.title: Hero image sequence or magazine spread
slides.copy: Use this for a short image story, featured campaign sequence, or homepage visual rhythm.

slides.title: Optional captions keep the gallery content-aware
slides.copy: A useful middle ground between a decorative slideshow and a full editorial section.

slides.title: Framework-free and spec-driven
slides.copy: The behavior is lightweight enough to stay native to Codette instead of importing a UI framework for one pattern.

sections.title: Keep the generator boring. Put the sophistication in the patterns.
sections.copy: The generator should mostly validate, render, and write files. That keeps the architecture stable while the pattern library grows through actual usage.
points: Each section pattern owns its markup and responsive behavior.
Themes define tokens, not content structure.
Site specs stay shallow enough for agents to edit confidently.

sections.quote: Small systems age better when they resist abstraction until reuse is obvious.

sections.title: Two-up promotional blocks cover events, press, products, or secondary offers.
sections.copy: This is the more reusable abstraction behind the alternating promo rows in Amplified Expansion Coaching.

items.title: Event or workshop feature
items.copy: Use this for a current event stream, gathering calendar, or time-sensitive offer that needs visual emphasis.

items.title: Press or coverage feature
items.copy: Use this for interviews, podcasts, media mentions, or partnership highlights without building a separate template.

sections.title: Signup bands should feel like a section, not an afterthought.
sections.copy: A useful baseline for newsletters, early access, communities, or lightweight lead capture.

sections.title: Contact blocks can stay crisp and composable.
sections.copy: This pattern turns the contact card cluster from Amplified Expansion Coaching into a reusable section contract.

footer.blurb: A lightweight static site system built for agentic frontend workflows.
